'''Louxin Zhang''' is a Canadian [[computational biologist]] and mathematician. He is a professor in the Department of Mathematics at the [[National University of Singapore]].<ref name="dnesg">{{Cite web |title=Louxin Zhang Profile {{!}} National University of Singapore |url=https://discovery.nus.edu.sg/822-louxin-zhang |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=discovery.nus.edu.sg}}</ref> 

His research interests include computational biology, [[bioinformatics]], and discrete mathematics.His work has examined topics in combinatorial [[Semigroup|semigroup theory]] as well as mathematical approaches to [[Phylogenetic tree|phylogenetic trees]] and [[Phylogenetic network|phylogenetic networks]]. Zhang has also contributed to research on spaced seeds used in sequence comparison methods within bioinformatics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home page |url=https://blog.nus.edu.sg/louxinzhang/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=blog.nus.edu.sg}}</ref>

==Early life==
Louxin Zhang was raised in [[Luoyang|Luoyang, Henan, China]]. He completed his undergraduate and master's degrees in mathematics at [[Lanzhou University]]. He later moved to Canada to pursue doctoral studies in computer science at the [[University of Waterloo]]. Zhang received his Ph.D. in computer science from the University of Waterloo with a dissertation titled "Emulations and Embeddings of Meshes of Trees and Hypercubes of Cliques.

==Career==
After completing postdoctoral research under [[Ming Li]], Zhang began his independent research career in 1996 at the [[Institute of Systems Science|Institute of Systems Sciences]], now part of the Institute for Infocomm Research. In 1997, he was awarded a three-year Lee Kuan Yew Postdoctoral Fellowship.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lee Kuan Yew Postdoctoral Fellowship |url=https://www.nus.edu.sg/research/research-management/funding-opportunities/lee-kuan-yew-postdoctoral-fellowship |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=NUS-ODPRT |language=en}}</ref> 

During his research career, Zhang has worked on topics in theoretical computer science and computational biology. His studies have introduced the application of string rewriting techniques to the word problem and [[conjugacy problem]] in special [[Monoid|monoids]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zhang |first=Louxin |date=November 1992 |title=Applying rewriting methods to special monoids |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-proceedings-of-the-cambridge-philosophical-society/article/abs/applying-rewriting-methods-to-special-monoids/BD174EDC8CE4178E5760879BB5035B63 |journal=[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]] |language=en |volume=112 |issue=3 |pages=495–505 |doi=10.1017/S0305004100071176 |bibcode=1992MPCPS.112..495Z |s2cid=15380487 |issn=1469-8064|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zhang |first=Louxin |date=1991-11-01 |title=Conjugacy in special monoids |journal=Journal of Algebra |language=en |volume=143 |issue=2 |pages=487–497 |doi=10.1016/0021-8693(91)90275-D |issn=0021-8693|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zhang |first=Louxin |date=1992-06-01 |title=On the conjugacy problem for one-relator monoids with elements of finite order |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S021819679200013X |journal=International Journal of Algebra and Computation |volume=02 |issue=2 |pages=209–220 |doi=10.1142/S021819679200013X |issn=0218-1967|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He has also conducted research on phylogenetic trees and phylogenetic networks, including work on the tree component decomposition method developed with collaborators.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gunawan |first1=Andreas D. M. |last2=DasGupta |first2=Bhaskar |last3=Zhang |first3=Louxin |date=2017-02-01 |title=A decomposition theorem and two algorithms for reticulation-visible networks |journal=Information and Computation |language=en |volume=252 |pages=161–175 |doi=10.1016/j.ic.2016.11.001 |issn=0890-5401|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Zhang’s work has additionally examined evolutionary models involving [[Human evolutionary genetics|gene loss]], gene duplication, and [[incomplete lineage sorting]]. The technique has been used to study problems related to tree containment, the exact and asymptotic counting of tree-child networks, and methods for inferring minimum phylogenies. His research has also addressed spaced seeds for sequence comparison and methods for reconstructing ancestral genome sequences.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zhang |first1=Louxin |last2=Abhari |first2=Niloufar |last3=Colijn |first3=Caroline |last4=Wu |first4=Yufeng |title=A fast and scalable method for inferring phylogenetic networks from trees by aligning lineage taxon strings |journal=Genome Research |date=July 2023 |volume=33 |issue=7 |pages=1053–1060 |doi=10.1101/gr.277669.123 |url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10538497/ |access-date=20 March 2026 |issn=1549-5469}}</ref>

Zhang has authored and co-authored a number of publications in the fields of computational biology, phylogenetics, and algorithm design. Selected works include:

M. |last2=DasGupta |first2=Bhaskar |last3=Zhang |first3=Louxin |date=2017-02-01 |title=A decomposition theorem and two algorithms for reticulation-visible networks |journal=Information and Computation |language=en |volume=252 |pages=161–175 |doi=10.1016/j.ic.2016.11.001 |issn=0890-5401|doi-access=free }}
